title: Learning to Evaluate: Cost-Effective Model Evaluation on Unlabeled Data with Meta-Learning

problem.claim: Assessing the reliability of newly released models on unseen and unlabeled data is increasingly difficult as model ecosystems expand.

gap.claim: Existing evaluation pipelines incur high costs through annotation and repeated fine-tuning or depend on assumptions that may not generalize to new models.

contributions.claim: MetaEvaluator is a cost-efficient, model-agnostic framework for rapidly assessing unseen models across varied architectures and modalities without labels.
MetaEvaluator meta-learns over reference models to obtain an initialization for assessing unseen models, amortizing evaluation cost and avoiding per-model retraining.
The work provides code for MetaEvaluator.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that MetaEvaluator is the first model-agnostic framework for evaluating new models on unlabeled datasets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments showing stable and accurate performance estimates at substantially lower cost than conventional approaches.
The authors report that MetaEvaluator enables scalable benchmarking on unlabeled datasets for emerging models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Model ecosystem growth makes reliability assessment on unseen and unlabeled data difficult.
Conventional evaluation relies on costly annotation, repeated fine-tuning, or weakly generalizing assumptions.
MetaEvaluator introduces model-agnostic, label-free evaluation using meta-learning over reference models.
The authors distinguish the framework as, to their knowledge, the first model-agnostic approach for evaluating new models on unlabeled datasets.
Reported experiments indicate accurate and stable estimates at lower cost and support scalable unlabeled-data benchmarking.

source_observation.claim: Meta-learning over reference models can provide an initialization for evaluating unseen models without per-model retraining.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation systems may reduce repeated adaptation costs by transferring learned evaluation knowledge across models.

application.claim: Use a reference-model pool to build scalable, label-free evaluation workflows for emerging models when labeled test data or retraining budgets are limited.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how well the approach transfers across specific architectures, modalities, or distribution shifts.

unknowns: Datasets, model pool composition, architectures, modalities, metrics, baselines, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The abstract does not quantify evaluation cost or define the conditions under which estimates are accurate and stable.
Limitations, failure cases, and reproducibility details beyond code availability are unspecified.
